positive_controls.argument: A defined actionable decision and response horizon give each proposed diagnostic measure an actual use and stop pointless measurement.
Configuration-bound integrated behavior supplies an observed diagnostic input beyond self-reported completion.
Risk-driven discrimination identifies consequential evidence worth measuring before dependent commitment.
A specific planning horizon and response decision provide the context in which a diagnostic metric has value.
A guarded interpretable experiment can test whether an apparent metric improvement corresponds to the intended decision effect.
Authoritative current intent identifies what the measure is meant to inform and which changed obligations alter its meaning.
An explicit learning action and decision consequence can test the uncertain proxy relation instead of treating dashboard conformity as truth.
A representative executable discriminator supplies operational observations that can challenge the metric’s claimed interpretation.
Representative use evidence tests whether the measured indicator corresponds to the outcome the regime claims to diagnose.
The actual accepted configuration, criteria and exceptions define the scope in which an acceptance-related measure may be interpreted.
Hazard and control analysis identifies consequential harms and exposures that the diagnostic measurement boundary must include.
Explicit claims and defeaters identify which metric assumptions matter and where contradictory evidence must remain visible.
Persistent anomaly state, affected configuration and residuals supply the diagnostic denominator and adverse evidence that closure counts omit.
The explicit commitment and decision criteria specify which measurements can actually change the go, redirect or stop decision.
Forecast ranges, reference-class challenge and target separation expose what the measurements do and do not predict.
The actual operating envelope and accepted residual conditions identify which monitored quantities are consequential.
Explicit consequence, recovery and observability dimensions identify meaningful countermetrics and the decision cost of measuring them.
